claims.text: FeCoNiCrAl powder with a 15–45 μm particle-size range was optimal for producing high-quality coatings with the HVAF-M3 system.
Default HVAF-i7 parameters produce acceptable-quality FeCoNiCrAl coatings but inadequate coating thickness.
Increasing the HVAF-i7 nozzle-to-substrate distance to approximately 350 mm will increase the velocity of 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl particles.
A longer spray distance gives particles a longer acceleration path and therefore additional kinetic energy.
Greater particle kinetic energy improves deformation and flattening on impact.
Improved particle deformation promotes stronger inter-splat bonding and coating densification.
Higher impact energy improves splat formation and bonding.
Higher impact energy causes rapid solidification that reduces exposure to oxidizing environments.
A 350 mm spray distance will produce a significantly thicker FeCoNiCrAl bond coat than the default HVAF-i7 distance.
A 350 mm spray distance will produce a more adherent FeCoNiCrAl bond coat than the default HVAF-i7 distance.
A 350 mm spray distance will reduce as-sprayed oxidation relative to the default HVAF-i7 distance.
The resulting coating will retain structural integrity and durability during elevated-temperature thermal-barrier service.
The intervention will remain effective under low-oxygen deposition conditions.
The approximately 350 mm standoff intervention will remain effective when coating internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
Monitoring in-flight particle velocity and temperature can ensure beneficial kinetic energy without excessive oxidation.

contradictions.description: The proposed 350 mm nozzle-to-substrate standoff is not geometrically reconciled with deposition on the interior wall of a 120 mm-diameter substrate. A special angled, axial, or remote-nozzle geometry would be required, but none is specified.
